author: reek
body: The state block carries the phase and the folded pointer: [0] phase, [4] x, [8] y, [12] buttons, [16] click edge (left button went down in the last consumed report), [20] event count (probe visibility).

author: reek
body: A machine can carry more than one boot-mouse interface, and the one a person moves is not obliged to be the first the walk meets -- the same defect the keyboard had, cured the same day it was proven on the ASUS (four keyboard-shaped interfaces, keys on the fourth). Peers each pump their own endpoint but fold into ONE position block (`um-pos`), because the desktop has one cursor: phase and the per-interface event count stay in the interface's own `um-state`, position, buttons and the click edge live at `um-pos`, which for the primary is its own state block and for every peer is the primary's.

author: reek
body: The deltas are signed 8-bit two's complement, and the folded position is clamped to the panel so the pointer parks at an edge instead of leaving the screen.

author: reek
body: The tail of the keyboard's endpoint bring-up, minted as a mouse. The pointer starts at the origin; the screen that adopts it warps it to wherever it wants the cursor born.

author: reek
body: The peer form skips SET_CONFIGURATION when the device is already configured (USB 2.0 9.1.1.5: re-sending it resets every data toggle the device holds) and folds into the position block it is handed; zero means own the position, the primary's case.

author: reek
body: Arm one interrupt IN transfer; check the event ring without blocking through the per-endpoint latch (another wait on the shared host may already have consumed this endpoint's completion -- on a combo receiver the keyboard pump polls this very slot); consume the report whole. Returns 1 exactly when a report was folded, so the caller knows to move the cursor.
